chapter: Cee Pee Johnson, Hampton and the Navy band
title: Daily routine at the Navy school
summary: Duties of flag raising, rehearsal and chow formation, and living off base for three years.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, that was a good band, had a lot of guys in it. I think I mentioned some of the names already. It was a nice experience. We lived in what we kind of called the country club of the Navy. Actually, our duties consisted of raising the flag in the morning and rehearsing most of the day, playing the chow formation for the cadets to walk to lunch, coming back and rehearsing and going home at night and sleeping at home.
You didn't have to live on base?

Didn't live on the base because they didn't have enough room for us. Thank God. So, they paid $106 a month for subsistence, so we rented our own place to stay in. So, I did that for three years and it was very comfortable in doing so.
